title: Thousands march in Bordeaux against cost of living and for public services

tea.why: Protesters marched to express anger over the high cost of living, declining purchasing power, and to defend public services.
tea.want: Demonstrators demanded better purchasing power, public service defense, ecological and economic transition, and action on living costs.
tea.changed: Nov 5: Thousands marched through Bordeaux in a mobilization called by trade unions, with some clashes reported after the event ended.

summary: Thousands of people took to the streets of Bordeaux on November 5, 2026, for a day of general strike and protests targeting the cost of living, falling purchasing power, and the defense of public services. Organised by an inter-union coalition, the march drew participants from various sectors including students, high schoolers, teachers, healthcare workers, and retirees. According to authorities, around 21,000 people participated, while union organizers claimed up to 120,000 attendees. The procession moved peacefully from Place de la République toward Place de la Victoire, though sources noted some clashes with law enforcement occurring more than an hour after the march concluded.
demands: Defend purchasing power and address the cost of living
Achieve generational justice and ecological transition
response: According to the sources, the prefecture approved a march route avoiding the hypercenter to protect businesses from potential vandalism. Clashes with law enforcement were reported after the protest ended.

updates.text: Thousands participated in a march across Bordeaux as part of a general strike day against the cost of living.
Reports noted that clashes with law enforcement broke out more than an hour after the official end of the demonstration at Place de la Victoire.
